title: Pay insurance duty on premiums (insurers)
what: An insurer pays duty on the premiums for the insurance it writes in the state, and usually passes it on to the insured.

sources.title: Duties Act 2008 (WA)
sources.quote: 213. Who is liable to pay duty Duty chargeable on the premium paid in relation to a contract of insurance is payable by — (a) the insurer — if the insurer is a general insurer; or (b) the insured person — if the insurer is not a general insurer.

sources.title: Duties Act 2008 (WA)
sources.locator: s 162, words naming the body (found 18 Nov 2026) (current version)
sources.quote: the Commissioner may determine that, despite that subsection, the persons are not related persons for the purposes of section 163.

confidence_note: The Act's own words make the insurer liable for the duty (in the NT, the quote is the duty to register as an insurer before writing dutiable policies).

assessment.summary: A tax on insurance premiums on top of GST. It discourages people and businesses from insuring and leaves more risk unpooled; the Henry Review recommended abolishing all such taxes.

marks.reason: Raises the price of insurance relative to other services, so people under-insure (Henry Review).

assessment.confidence_note: The direction is well supported; no official estimate of the efficiency cost of insurance duty was found. Marks copied from the register item wa-insurance-duty so the two agree.
